title: ReAct: Reasoning + Acting
hook: Thinking alone can drift; acting alone is blind. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool calls so an LLM can plan, look things up, and correct course — the template for agents.
key_points: Interleaves reasoning traces ('thoughts') with actions like tool calls and searches.
Lets the model gather external information instead of relying on memory alone.
Observations from actions feed back into the next round of reasoning.
Reduces hallucination versus reasoning with no grounding.
A foundational loop behind modern LLM agents.
content_html: ReAct, from Yao, Zhao, and colleagues in 2022, combines two things LLMs do well separately: reasoning in words and taking actions. The model alternates between writing a thought and performing an action — like searching a knowledge source — then uses what it observes to inform the next thought. This loop lets it plan, fetch facts, and adjust as it goes.
extra_html:
How it works

At each step the model emits either a thought (free-form reasoning about what to do) or an action (a tool call, such as a search query). The environment returns an observation, which gets appended to the running context. The model reads that result and decides its next thought or action, repeating until it can produce an answer. Reasoning guides which actions to take, and actions supply grounding the reasoning can't invent.

Why it matters

Pure chain-of-thought reasoning can confidently go off the rails because nothing checks it against the real world. By weaving in actions that pull in real information, ReAct keeps the model honest and lets it solve tasks that need external knowledge or steps. This thought-action-observation cycle became a foundational pattern for the LLM agents that browse, query tools, and complete multi-step tasks today.
